items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I think I heard Louis Armstrong say a couple of times... I connect one thing to another and it carried all the way through to Louis Armstrong you know... I was interested in antique music, you know, 'Muskrat Ramble' and Louis Armstrong Hot Fives and Sevens.

ctx.x: Yeah, the “Pennies From Heaven” type of songs.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. So it was all around me, and I wasn’t necessarily in the cradle of the blues or anything like that. But that’s a funny one. I mean you’ll hear young black guys, I have my own ideas about the origin of jazz, I don’t think it’s black. It’s not a black music, it’s an American music. There was always white and Irishmen and Italians and stuff. And if you’re black and you want to be proud about your black rhythm, that’s marvelous, that’s great, some of the greatest were you know. Joe Oliver, Louis…
